scenes.heading: Replication Agents and Queues in 6.5
scenes.narration: Oak & Operations. Replication Agents and Queues in 6.5. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: Which agents are part of a standard AEM 6.5 installation?
scenes.heading: The Default Agent, Dispatcher Flush, Reverse Replication, and the Static Agent
scenes.body: Section 10 says a standard 6.5 installation has the Default Agent for Author to Publish, Dispatcher Flush, Reverse Replication, and the Static Agent.

scenes.question: What do the queue states Active, Idle, and Blocked mean?
scenes.heading: Active means items are being processed, Idle means the queue is empty, and Blocked means items are queued but cannot be processed
scenes.body: The source defines Active, Idle, and Blocked exactly in terms of processing items, emptiness, and queued items that cannot be processed.

scenes.question: What is the default Retry Delay for a replication agent in AEM 6.5?
scenes.heading: 60000 milliseconds
scenes.body: Section 10 says agent settings include Retry Delay with a default of 60000 milliseconds.

scenes.question: What access must the Agent User Id have, and what happens if it is left empty?
scenes.heading: It needs read access to all replicated paths on Author and create/write access on Publish; if empty, the system user is used

scenes.question: Which log levels are available for a replication agent, and what is the default?
scenes.heading: Error, Info, and Debug, with Info as the default

scenes.heading: bin/receive
